$comment: MACHINE-READABLE RULES REQUIREMENT — HANDOFF, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION.
This repository does not own a canonical firestore.rules file: firebase.json here has no
'firestore' section, and .emulator-local/firestore.rules is untracked local scratch (it also
still contains a God-Mode identity backdoor and a status denylist, and must not be treated as
the contract). The rules owner is the mobile/backend lane. This file states exactly what those
rules must enforce and how to test it, so the requirement can be applied without re-deriving it.
Nothing here has been deployed, and no rules file has been modified by this lane.
v2.0.0 strengthens this from a description into a machine-verifiable contract:
every collection now declares its permitted server projection, the role/status required to
reach it through a callable, and the aliases/alternate paths that must NOT bypass it.
scripts/outreach-production-binding-verify.mjs enforces the parts that are checkable from
this repository; the rules themselves remain the owning lane's to apply.
rationale: These five collections are SERVER-OWNED. Every read and write is performed by Cloud Functions
through the Firebase Admin SDK, which bypasses security rules entirely, so denying all direct
client access costs the product nothing and removes the entire client attack surface.
They carry approval authority (who approved what, at which version, under which digest) and
outreach draft text. A client that could write them could forge an approval; a client that
could read them could read draft content scoped to someone else.

collections.notes: Client reads must be denied even for staff: the server projection scopes draft content to the creator and assigned reviewer, and a direct read would bypass that scoping.
collections.projectionScoping: subject and body are returned ONLY to the record creator or the assigned reviewer; every other active staff member receives null for both.

collections.notes: Append-only. No client, including staff, may create, update or delete a receipt.
collections.projectionScoping: not projected to any client by any callable in this lane.

carries: replay ledger: command fingerprint and stored outcome
collections.notes: A client that could write this could forge a replayed success for a command it never made.
A client write here would let a caller lift their own legal hold. Absence of a document means NOT held; a failed read means UNKNOWN and blocks.
collections.projectionScoping: exposed only as the boolean/null hold state on a draft row.

collections.notes: A client write here would manufacture legal approval for a jurisdiction counsel has not approved.
collections.projectionScoping: exposed only as a boolean on a draft row; the approval version is not projected.
collections.requiredCallerRole: Director for any future write path

requiredRule.form: explicit deny for every operation, placed so no earlier broader match can grant access
requiredRule.placement: Must not be shadowed by a preceding wildcard match such as /{document=**} that allows staff reads. Verify with the rules simulator that an authenticated staff account is denied.

testContract.notes: Staff too. The callable is the only authorized path, because it applies content scoping.
A direct write would bypass the digest, version and separation-of-duties checks.
Receipts are append-only; deletion must be impossible from any client.
Forging a ledger entry would let a caller be served a success for a command never made.
Otherwise a caller can lift the hold that blocks them.
Legal approval is not a thing any client may assert.
Admin SDK bypasses rules by design; this entry records the intended server path, not a rule to write.
A single-path match rule does not cover collection-group reads; this needs its own denial.
A nested copy must not be readable.
Suspended staff have no path at all, callable or direct.
The legacy shape the old denylist admitted must be denied here too.

verifiedByThisLane.notes: Both properties are asserted on every gate run. This lane cannot verify the rules themselves, because it does not own a rules file.

handoff.action: Apply requiredRule to the canonical firestore.rules and add testContract R1-R15 to the rules test suite. Cover the alternate paths in aliasAndAlternatePathControls.
handoff.blocking: Until applied, these collections rely solely on the absence of client code that reads them — which is a convention, not a control.

aliasAndAlternatePathControls.rationale: A deny rule on an exact collection path is bypassed by any other path that reaches the same data: a collection-group query, a differently-cased or pluralized alias, a nested subcollection, or a client constant that spells the name indirectly.

forbiddenAlternatePaths.requirement: must be denied; a collection-group query is not covered by a single-path match rule
must be denied; nesting must not create a readable copy
no such collection may be created; Firestore paths are case-sensitive so an alias is a distinct, unruled collection
client code must not construct these names at all, directly or by concatenation
no mirror may be created without extending this contract

verifiedHere: no client file names any of the five collections
no client file constructs a collection name by concatenation of the enterprise_ prefix
no collectionGroup query names any of the five collections anywhere in the repository
